laws.rule: Don't use or carry illegal drugs. Penalties for drug offences are severe. Possessing even small amounts of illegal drugs can lead to prison sentences. This includes marijuana.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: You must carry your ID at all times. It's illegal to photograph military and police: personnel buildings vehicles equipment
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: For specific information on bringing medication into Bosnia and Herzegovina, visit the Embassy or consulate of Bosnia and Herzegovina website.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: You can drive on your Australian driver's licence for up to 6 months. You'll need both: a current Australian driver's licence (digital driver’s licences may not be accepted) a valid international driving permit (IDP) Driving without an IDP could void your travel and vehicle insurance. Get your IDP before departing Australia. The minimum age for driving is 18 years old.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: You need the correct insurance cover to enter Bosnia and Herzegovina in a vehicle. If you don't, border police will direct you to an insurer at the border crossing to buy insurance. If travelling by car, research and prepare before entry. Not all border crossings have an insurer's office, and credit card payments aren't always possible.
laws.heading: Driver's insurance

laws.rule: Non-commercial (Open) flights: daylight and within sight only; up to 30 m above ground; at least 30 m from people, animals, structures and roads, 50 m from public gatherings, 500 m from industrial zones, embassies and government buildings; no flying over people; insurance for drones over 1 kg. Not from within 300 m of the border without Border Police consent. Drones over 25 kg need special BHDCA approval.
laws.heading: Drone rules (Rulebook 51/20)

laws.rule: Travellers bringing in or taking out cash or securities worth more than EUR 10,000 (about A$15,900 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293) must declare it at every border crossing, on a Cash Declaration Form. The page lists no penalty.
laws.heading: Cash declaration

laws.rule: The Indirect Taxation Authority lists per day: 1 litre of spirits over 22% alcohol; 2 litres at 22% or below; 4 litres of still wine; 16 litres of beer. Travellers under 17 get no exemption.
laws.heading: Alcohol allowance on entry

laws.rule: The Indirect Taxation Authority lists per day up to 200 cigarettes, or 100 cigarillos, or 50 cigars, or 250 g of smoking tobacco, or a proportional mix. Travellers under 17 get no exemption. The page does not mention e-cigarettes.
laws.heading: Tobacco allowance on entry

laws.rule: The page says personal consignments of meat and dairy are allowed from listed countries, including EU countries, with exceptions for powdered infant milk and certain special foods; larger consignments need veterinary inspection and a health certificate. It says not declaring such consignments is punishable. Check the page for the list of countries.
laws.heading: Meat and dairy

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Destination Sarajevo: religious sites are open to visitors in modest dress (at mosques women in trousers or a long skirt with arms covered and a scarf over the head, men with shoulders covered and trousers below the knee); shoes off on entering a mosque; photography is unacceptable only during prayer. Guests usually remove shoes in homes and are offered coffee first. Always carry your passport or official photo ID, including for hotel check-in. During Ramadan check opening hours and follow local dress codes. LGBT+ communities report discrimination and violence; public affection is likely to attract negative attention. Drug penalties are severe.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: BHDCA's Rulebook (Official Gazette of BiH 51/20) splits drone use into Open, Specific (commercial) and Certified (aerial work); aerial work needs special BHDCA approval. No public operator register was found.

items.text: No public operator register was found on the BHDCA drone page.

Commercial operations fall in the Specific category, with daylight visual line of sight, insurance for third-party damage whatever the drone's mass, a 30 m lateral distance from people and structures, and a maximum altitude of 120 m. Aerial work (Certified) needs special approval: contact BHDCA at the drone address on the page before starting.
The page does not set a separate foreign-operator route; it says drones under foreign institutions (army, police, customs) need approval from the competent Bosnian institution first.
